## Proof

**Claim:** The cardinality of the set of hyperreal numbers ${}^*\mathbb{R}$ is $2^{\aleph_0}$, the cardinality of the continuum.

**Construction.** The hyperreal numbers are standardly constructed as the ultrapower
$${}^*\mathbb{R} = \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}} / \mathcal{U},$$
where $\mathcal{U}$ is a free (nonprincipal) ultrafilter on $\mathbb{N}$, and two sequences $x, y \in \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ are identified ($x \sim y$) when $\{n \in \mathbb{N} : x_n = y_n\} \in \mathcal{U}$.

**Upper bound.** The set of representatives is $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$, so
$$|{}^*\mathbb{R}| \le |\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}| = |\mathbb{R}|^{|\mathbb{N}|} = (2^{\aleph_0})^{\aleph_0} = 2^{\aleph_0 \cdot \aleph_0} = 2^{\aleph_0}.$$
Thus $|{}^*\mathbb{R}| \le 2^{\aleph_0}$.

**Lower bound.** There is a canonical embedding $\iota: \mathbb{R} \to {}^*\mathbb{R}$ sending each real $r$ to the equivalence class of the constant sequence $(r, r, r, \dots)$. This map is injective: if $r \neq s$, then $\{n : r = s\} = \varnothing \notin \mathcal{U}$ (since $\mathcal{U}$ is free, it contains no finite set, in particular not $\varnothing$), so the constant sequences are not identified. Hence
$$|{}^*\mathbb{R}| \ge |\mathbb{R}| = 2^{\aleph_0}.$$

**Conclusion.** Combining both bounds,
$$|{}^*\mathbb{R}| = 2^{\aleph_0}.$$

The set of hyperreal numbers has the same cardinality as the continuum, namely $2^{\aleph_0}$ (equivalently, $\mathfrak{c}$).

### PROOF COMPLETE
